narrative:
The model estimates a 60% chance that you will leave your current job. Because of this, the company has decided not to offer you the promotion at this time.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this prediction were your overall years of experience, the length of time you have spent in your current role, and whether you had received other job offers while working here. 

Your total professional experience of 6–10 years pushed the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expected to stay, half had only 1–5 years of experience, so your longer track record made you appear more likely to move on. Similarly, having spent 6–10 years in this organization also leaned the prediction toward departure; most people the model predicted would stay had been at their company for fewer than six years.

On the positive side, the fact that you had not received other job offers while here worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward staying. However, this single positive influence was not enough to outweigh the combined effect of your experience levels.

The organization should consider discussing your career goals with you openly and exploring whether additional responsibilities or changes in role could increase your sense of stability and satisfaction. You may also want to reflect on what would make staying with the company more appealing in the long term.
